output.answer: Yes. LinkedIn announced layoffs on May 13, 2026 — its most recent round as of November 11, 2026 — cutting about 5% of its roughly 17,500-person workforce (approximately 875 roles) as it reorganizes teams toward its growing business areas. LinkedIn confirmed the cuts via a spokesperson ("As part of our regular business planning, we've implemented organizational changes to best position ourselves for future success"), and an internal memo from CEO Daniel Shapero said the company would scale back marketing campaigns, vendor spend, customer events and underutilized office space, including closing its Graz, Austria office. California WARN filings later showed 606 LinkedIn employees notified of permanent layoffs effective July 13, 2026. No newer LinkedIn layoff announcement has been reported since that May round.
caveats: LinkedIn never disclosed an exact headcount for the cuts; the ~875-role figure is Reuters'/The Verge's estimate of 5% of LinkedIn's roughly 17,500-person workforce, and LinkedIn declined to provide specific numbers.
The 606-worker figure from WARN filings covers only California employees; the global total affected may be higher, and Reuters reported it was unable to determine which teams were affected.
As of November 11, 2026, no announcement of a newer LinkedIn layoff round has been found — the May 13, 2026 cuts remain the most recent — but this could change.

passages.quote:
SAN FRANCISCO, May 13 (Reuters) - LinkedIn planned to inform staff of layoffs on Wednesday, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a widening of technology ​sector cuts this year.

The Microsoft-owned [(MSFT.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/MSFT.O) social network plans to cut about ​5% of its headcount as it reorganizes teams and focuses personnel on areas ⁠where its business is growing, said one of the people, on condition ​of anonymity.

Microsoft starts layoffs at LinkedIn.

Microsoft is reportedly cutting around five percent of its LinkedIn headcount this week, approximately 875 roles. [_Reuters_ reports](https://www.reuters.com/business/world-at-work/linkedin-is-planning-lay-off-5-staff-latest-tech-sector-cuts-source-says-2026-05-13/) that Microsoft-owned LinkedIn will inform staff of the cuts today. Microsoft confirmed the layoffs in a statement to _[Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4592192-microsoft-owned-linkedin-plans-to-reduce-staff-in-latest-tech-sector-layoff)_. “As part of our regular business planning, we’ve implemented organizational changes to best position ourselves for future success,” said an unnamed LinkedIn spokesperson.

LinkedIn is laying off employees, according to an internal memo viewed by Business Insider sent by CEO Daniel Shapero.

Impacted employees would receive a calendar invite within an hour of Shapero's email being sent at 7 a.m. Pacific, according to the memo. Roles include those in the Microsoft-owned company's Global Business Organization, marketing, engineering, and product teams.

It's unclear how many employees would be impacted by this round of layoffs. LinkedIn employs around 17,500 workers.

The company will also "scale back investments" in areas including marketing campaigns, vendor spend, customer events, and underutilized office space, according to the memo.

"As part of our regular business planning, we've implemented organizational changes to best position ourselves for future success," a LinkedIn spokesperson told Business Insider.

Employees in Asia and the Pacific would learn whether they were affected on Thursday, according to a separate memo. LinkedIn is also closing its office in Graz, Austria, as part of the cost-cutting.

Hundreds of [LinkedIn employees](https://nypost.com/business/linkedin-hiring-alternatives/) will be looking for work this summer, with over 600 workers set to be laid off in the months ahead.

A new Worker Accounting and Retraining Notification (WARN) report reveals that 606 LinkedIn employees were notified of [permanent layoffs](https://nypost.com/2026/04/22/business/bloodbath-at-mark-zuckerberg-backed-california-school-as-tech-titan-and-his-wife-strip-funding/) last week, which will go into effect on July 13.

The bulk of the layoffs (352) come from their Mountain View, California office, with another 66 [remote employees](https://nypost.com/2026/05/08/lifestyle/top-20-high-paying-remote-jobs-that-dont-require-degrees/) in the same city.

Another 108 employees were laid off at their San Francisco office, plus another 59 at their Sunnyvale office and 21 in Carpinteria.

LinkedIn Corporation has 5 WARN notices dated in the 12 months to November 9, 2026, naming 606 workers.

Source: [WARN Notice Register](https://bchaps1999.github.io/warn-notice-register/). [See the notices and their source links](https://groundworkpay.com/layoffs/linkedin#notices).

output.question: Has LinkedIn announced layoffs?

key_facts.fact: Reuters exclusively reported LinkedIn planned to cut about 5% of its headcount (out of more than 17,500 full-time workers) as it reorganizes teams and focuses personnel on growth areas; Reuters sources said the rationale was not AI replacing jobs, and LinkedIn revenue rose 12% year-over-year in the just-ended quarter per Microsoft's filings.

Microsoft confirmed the LinkedIn layoffs (about five percent of LinkedIn headcount, approximately 875 roles) in a statement to Seeking Alpha: "As part of our regular business planning, we've implemented organizational changes to best position ourselves for future success."

An internal memo from LinkedIn CEO Daniel Shapero (his first major restructuring since becoming CEO in April 2026) said layoffs would hit the Global Business Organization, marketing, engineering and product teams; the company would also scale back investments in marketing campaigns, vendor spend, customer events and underutilized office space, and close its Graz, Austria office. LinkedIn declined to say how many employees were affected.

A California WARN report showed 606 LinkedIn employees were notified of permanent layoffs effective July 13, 2026: 352 at the Mountain View office, 66 remote employees in Mountain View, 108 in San Francisco, 59 in Sunnyvale and 21 in Carpinteria.

The WARN Notice Register shows LinkedIn Corporation had 5 WARN notices dated in the 12 months to November 9, 2026, naming 606 workers (versus 4 notices / 281 workers in the prior 12 months), confirming no new US layoff notices beyond the May 2026 round as of November 2026.
